original_question: If x_1, ..., x_n are linearly independent over Q, must the field Q(x_1, ..., x_n, e^{x_1}, ..., e^{x_n}) have transcendence degree at least n?
target_in_paper: §3.1, Conjecture 3.1 (Schanuel). Your draft is targeting the paper’s exact formulation of Schanuel’s conjecture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content correctly: the hypothesis is Q-linear independence of x_1,...,x_n; the field is generated over Q by x_1,...,x_n together with e^{x_1},...,e^{x_n}; and the claimed lower bound is n for the transcendence degree. It also correctly avoids adding extra algebraicity assumptions, so it matches Schanuel’s full conjecture rather than the special case about logarithms of algebraic numbers. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
missing_details: The paper states explicitly that x_1,...,x_n are complex numbers. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))

The transcendence degree is explicitly over Q; just before Conjecture 3.1 the paper defines trdeg_k K and says that when k=Q it writes simply trdeg K. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
The quantifiers should be made explicit: for every positive integer n and every n-tuple x_1,...,x_n satisfying the Q-linear independence hypothesis. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
The exponential is the usual complex exponential, written in the section as e^z = exp(z). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))

As a stand-alone paper-faithful question, it should be identified as an open conjecture, namely Schanuel’s Conjecture (Conjecture 3.1), not as an established theorem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
refined_question: Schanuel’s Conjecture: For every positive integer n and every n-tuple x_1,...,x_n of Q-linearly independent complex numbers, must the field Q(x_1,...,x_n,e^{x_1},...,e^{x_n}) have transcendence degree at least n over Q, where e^z=exp(z)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
justification: The paper’s exact matching statement is Conjecture 3.1 in §3.1, which says precisely that Q-linearly independent complex numbers x_1,...,x_n should give trdeg_Q Q(x_1,...,x_n,e^{x_1},...,e^{x_n}) at least n. The nearby context supplies the notation for transcendence degree and the convention that trdeg means transcendence degree over Q. The neighboring items confirm the scope: Conjecture 3.2 is a separate Roy reformulation mentioned nearby, while Conjecture 3.3 is only a special case concerning logarithms of algebraic numbers, so the narrowest paper-faithful rewrite is simply the exact Schanuel formulation itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0312440))
